currentContext.strategies: Deepen AI integration across the platform portfolio (Wisely ATP, Wisely.ai, Wisely Communicate, Identity+) to sustain differentiation in trust and security within digital communications|Extend AI-led customer engagement capabilities beyond large enterprises to unlock the small and medium business (SMB) segment through scalable solutions|Continue platform innovation and new-use-case development, building on the commercialisation track record of Trubloq, MaaP and Wisely AI over the past five years|Leverage two decades of telecom and enterprise domain leadership, including government partnerships such as the Tamil Nadu e-Governance Agency's Namma Arasu WhatsApp-based governance initiative, to expand citizen-centric digital governance use cases|Grow international presence in Southeast Asia and the UAE, building on lessons from the Wisely.ai deployment with Indosat in Indonesia|Build a more balanced, diverse workforce with women representation targeted at 24% of the permanent workforce by FY30, supported by diversity-linked hiring goals and campus recruitment pipelines
currentContext.expansion: As an asset-light software/CPaaS platform company, Tanla's 'expansion' is largely geographic and infrastructural rather than physical capacity. It is extending its AI-native platforms (Wisely.ai, Wisely Communicate) to telcos across Southeast Asia and EMEA, building on its multi-year SaaS deployment with Indosat Ooredoo Hutchison in Indonesia (over 100 million subscribers protected, built on NVIDIA Blackwell GPU infrastructure within Indosat's sovereign AI factory), and describes a 'growing pipeline of engagements' in these new geographies. On the infrastructure side, the company has undertaken a data-centre and IT modernization programme: migrating ~90% of legacy physical servers to virtualised environments, deploying chassis-based integrated power/cooling modules, upgrading internal LAN to 10G networking, and moving from rated-power to metered power billing. A structural feasibility evaluation for a rooftop solar installation at the Hyderabad SEZ campus (its largest electricity-consuming site, ~36% of total grid electricity consumption) was completed in FY26, with commissioning targeted for FY27; the company is also evaluating open-access/green-tariff renewable procurement for its leased Chennai, Bengaluru and Mumbai campuses where rooftop installation is not feasible.

risks.note: Reviewed by the Risk Management Committee as a material business risk with direct implications for operations, reputation and compliance; AI-enabled attack methods are making threats faster and harder to detect, and the Committee assessed whether threat monitoring, security testing and incident response protocols would hold under a real-world attack scenario.

risks.risk: Third-party and platform dependency (telecom, cloud and technology partners)
risks.note: A third-party service disruption can cascade into a platform-availability problem; the Committee examined whether vendor governance and contractual safeguards are sufficient to protect service continuity if a critical partner is disrupted.

risks.risk: Shifting regulatory landscape across telecom, data protection and digital platforms
risks.note: Regulatory expectations continue to shift; management presents impact assessments for the most material regulatory changes and outlines structured response plans to the Risk Management Committee.

Flagged as a standing organisational risk given the competitive talent market and the demands of Tanla's ongoing transformation; the Committee reviewed whether succession planning and the leadership pipeline are deep enough for critical roles.
The Committee assessed progress on platform modernisation and decommissioning of legacy components, questioning whether the pace of change is sufficient to support Tanla's growth trajectory.

risks.risk: AI governance risk (internal adoption and external AI-enabled threats)
risks.note: Internally, focus is on data handling and model governance as AI adoption scales; externally, AI is making attack methods faster and harder to detect, requiring the platforms to stay structurally ahead of the threat curve.

risks.risk: Business continuity and disaster recovery for critical platforms
risks.note: The Committee reviewed preparedness for disruption to critical platforms and infrastructure, including recovery objectives, testing schedules and prioritisation of services for accelerated recovery in a real disruption scenario.

one-line thesis: Tanla reported stabilizing EBITDA margins (~16%) despite heavy GTM/AI investments, with the Digital Platform segment acting as the high-margin growth engine (98.2% gross margin) driven by new ATP bank wins (Bandhan) and global telco deployments. While SMS faces pricing pressure, the strategic pivot to utility-based OTT and subscription-model AI platforms positions the company for accelerated growth in FY27, offsetting a one-off ₹12 Cr FX loss.
financial scorecard: Revenue: FY26 Digital Platform ₹395 Cr (single-digit growth); Enterprise OTT run-rate ~₹1,000 Cr. EBITDA/Margin: Stabilized ~16% (conscious GTM/AI investment); Gross Margin improved slightly. PAT: Impacted by ₹12 Cr non-cash FX mark-to-market loss on specific liability. Order Book: 3 ATP bank deals live (incl. Bandhan), 5-year subscription contracts. Net Debt: Net Cash position (~₹1,000 Cr cash); no debt mentioned. One-offs: ₹12 Cr FX loss due to USD-INR fluctuation on unhedged balance sheet item.
guidance: Revenue Growth: >10% YoY expected (outpacing industry 8-10%); Digital Platform to accelerate in FY27/FY28. Margin: EBITDA to hold/improve as GTM investments bear fruit; UAE subsidiary gross margin improved to ~22%. Order Inflow: Huge pipeline for global telco ATP deals; focusing on SME market for OTT. Capex: Steady trajectory of ₹100-150 Cr per annum.
order book & pipeline: 3 live ATP bank contracts (5-year tenure, per-subscriber pricing); Indosat (Indonesia) deal live (100M subscribers); Pipeline for additional global telcos and banks.
segment / subsidiary detail: Enterprise: 75-80% revenue from top 250 clients; OTT share stable at ~31-32% due to mix shift from high-value promotional to lower-value utility messages. Digital Platforms: ₹395 Cr revenue; 98.2% gross margin; Wisely AI growing fast but base traditional products steady. International: UAE subsidiary (ValueFirst) revenue ~₹150-170 Cr, gross margin expanded to ~22%.
growth verticals / optionality: Launch of 'gigantic' new AI platform in Q1 FY27; Expansion of ATP to more banks/global telcos; Penetration of SME market via WhatsApp (2M target); Consolidation of UAE subsidiary expected in Q1 FY27.
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA pressure from deliberate GTM and R&D (AI) spend; SMS pricing erosion offset by volume growth; OTT blended realization softening due to regulatory push on utility vs promotional messages.
capex / expansion: ₹100-150 Cr annually expected to continue; focused on platform development and global expansion.
capital allocation: Shareholder returns via dividends and buybacks; M&A approach is 'build vs buy' due to high AI valuations, though open to right opportunities; no immediate plans for demerger/listing of platform business.
risks & watch-items: Regulatory changes (UPI/SMS notification norms); Pricing pressure in SMS; Delay in UAE subsidiary consolidation (regulatory approvals); FX volatility on unhedged liabilities.
management quality / tone: Confident on long-term AI/platform strategy; Transparent on margin compression being investment-led; Committed to closing UAE deal in Q1 FY27; Cautious on M&A valuations.
non-obvious takeaways: OTT revenue growth appears flat (~31% share) not due to lack of volume growth, but due to a structural mix shift from expensive 'promotional' messages to cheaper 'utility' messages driven by Meta's policy and customer experience focus; this masks underlying volume strength.

themes.title: Digital platforms, SaaS, payments & cybersecurity
themes.need: Digital-public-infrastructure scale, enterprise SaaS and a compliance/security upcycle drive a distinct platform cohort. PINELABS/NPST/CMSINFO on payments; AURIONPRO/NEWGEN/NUCLEUS/ROUTE/TANLA on banking/CPaaS software; EMUDHRA/META(544441)/AURIONPRO on digital-identity & cybersecurity; CAPILLARY/MAPMYINDIA/NAZARA on SaaS/geospatial/gaming. Q1FY27 anchored the payments leg: PAYTM's GMV grew 31% YoY (accelerating 23% -> 27% -> 31%) with merchant payments about 80% of the financial-services mix and 25-30 lakh device additions a year on a distribution-only lending model (no book, no FLDG); MOBIKWIK posted payments GMV of INR 52,400cr (+58% YoY), a 13th consecutive record quarter and India's largest wallet by GTV at ~20% share, against only ~INR 3,200cr of digital-credit GMV. OFSS adds the banking-software annuity, with RPO +17% YoY versus revenue +7% and licence-and-cloud revenue +13% at a 44% operating margin.
themes.driver: Deal/ARR additions; festive digital-payments TPV; merchant-device additions; RBI/regulatory compliance-driven security spend.

themes.title: Telecom & digital-infrastructure capex
themes.need: 5G monetization, FTTH and tower/fibre densification drive the connectivity cycle - and Q1FY27 repriced the optical leg outright. STLTECH booked order intake of INR 13,100cr in ONE quarter, 1.7x its entire FY26 order book, anchored by a multi-year $1.1bn hyperscaler deal running through FY29, taking the open order book to INR 18,618cr (up 2.4x QoQ) on revenue of INR 1,910cr (+87%) and EBITDA INR 397cr (+184%). It then raised guidance twice on the same call - EBITDA margin target from 20%-by-end-FY27 (already hit at 20.8% in Q1) to 23%, and Data-Center + Enterprise mix from 30% to 50% of FY27 revenue, after DC went from 1% of revenue in FY26 to 21%. The catch is supply, not demand: ex the anchor deal quarterly intake fell to ~INR 3,000cr from INR 7,000-8,000cr because 'we have to pick and choose the orders basis the capacity availability', with germanium and helium named as binding raw-material constraints. BHARTIARTL on ARPU + 5G; INDUSTOWER on tower rollout; SUYOG-tier on passive infra; GTPL/HFCL-tier on broadband + fibre; tariff hikes and rural FTTH are the near-term levers.
themes.driver: STLTECH's $1.1bn hyperscaler ramp against germanium/helium supply constraints and the raised 23% margin / 50% DC-mix guides; tariff-hike flow-through; 5G/FTTH capex; tower tenancy adds.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Tanla operates through two segments: Digital Platforms, which builds AI-native solutions (Wisely.ai, Wisely ATP, Trubloq, Identity+) that protect users from spam, scams and fraudulent interactions and let telcos and enterprises operate securely and compliantly; and Enterprise Communications, which lets enterprises engage customers across channels (SMS, WhatsApp, Google RCS, Truecaller, Email, Voice) via its go-to-market arms Karix and ValueFirst. demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Non-discretionary digital communication usage (banking alerts, UPI notifications, OTP volumes) continues to rise with the scale of India's digital economy, led by BFSI, government and other regulated sectors
- Discretionary spend in retail and e-commerce remains strong, with enterprises increasingly directing budgets toward AI-led solutions across the customer lifecycle
- OTT channels are opening new use cases for small and mid-sized businesses, broadening the addressable opportunity
- Intensifying regulatory focus on data security and privacy is creating greenfield opportunities in trusted communication that are still forming
- Digital communication is shifting from multichannel engagement to AI-native, outcome-driven experiences, with enterprises consolidating spend toward fewer, more capable unified platforms
- WhatsApp remains the fastest-growing channel; OTT channels now contribute approximately 50% of India's CPaaS mix
- India's CPaaS market is estimated at approximately INR 14,500 Cr (USD 1.7 billion), growing 5-7% annually; the global CPaaS market is projected to reach USD 27.4 billion by 2029 (Gartner)
- Rising trust deficit from spam, fraud and phishing is pushing enterprises toward secure, authenticated, compliant communication platforms

It is extending its AI-native platforms (Wisely.ai, Wisely Communicate) to telcos across Southeast Asia and EMEA, building on its multi-year SaaS deployment with Indosat Ooredoo Hutchison in Indonesia (over 100 million subscribers protected, built on NVIDIA Blackwell GPU infrastructure within Indosat's sovereign AI factory), and describes a 'growing pipeline of engagements' in these new geographies. On the infrastructure side, the company has undertaken a data-centre and IT modernization programme: migrating ~90% of legacy physical servers to virtualised environments, deploying chassis-based integrated power/cooling modules, upgrading internal LAN to 10G networking, and moving from rated-power to metered power billing. A structural feasibility evaluation for a rooftop solar installation at the Hyderabad SEZ campus (its largest electricity-consuming site, ~36% of total grid electricity consumption) was completed in FY26, with commissioning targeted for FY27; the company is also evaluating open-access/green-tariff renewable procurement for its leased Chennai, Bengaluru and Mumbai campuses where rooftop installation is not feasible.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- AI-native technological moat: AI embedded as the core architecture across all platforms (Wisely ATP, Wisely.ai, Wisely Communicate) for real-time threat detection, encryption and network-level optimization, described by management as an insurmountable moat versus legacy competitors
- Innovation track record: successfully deployed and commercialised Trubloq, MaaP and Wisely AI over the past five years, backed by eight patents filed to date
- Deep domain leadership and telecom integration built over two decades, including operating Trubloq for the Indian national switch processing over 70% of A2P transactions; 8% of workforce has 20+ years of specialised experience
- Deep, long-standing customer relationships: serves 70% of leading brands in India, with over 60% of revenue from customers with a relationship vintage of more than five years
- Debt-free balance sheet with strong free cash flow conversion (above 75% of PAT over the last three years), providing resilience and capacity to reinvest in innovation and expansion
- Global scale via go-to-market engines Karix (850+ Bn interactions processed annually, among the world's largest enterprise communication platforms) and ValueFirst, recognized as Google's RCS Growth/Anchor Partner two years running
- Recognised innovation leadership: named a Gartner CPaaS Visionary for the fourth consecutive year (2023-2026); S&P Global ESG score of 80 (100th percentile, Software industry topper)
- Proven international replication model demonstrated in Indonesia (Wisely.ai deployed with Indosat, protecting 100 million users and flagging over 2 billion spam/scam communications in six months), used as the template for further geographic expansion

risks.body: Regulatory changes (UPI/SMS notification norms); Pricing pressure in SMS; Delay in UAE subsidiary consolidation (regulatory approvals); FX volatility on unhedged liabilities.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: OTT revenue growth appears flat (~31% share) not due to lack of volume growth, but due to a structural mix shift from expensive 'promotional' messages to cheaper 'utility' messages driven by Meta's policy and customer experience focus; this masks underlying volume strength.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Deepen AI integration across the platform portfolio (Wisely ATP, Wisely.ai, Wisely Communicate, Identity+) to sustain differentiation in trust and security within digital communications
- Extend AI-led customer engagement capabilities beyond large enterprises to unlock the small and medium business (SMB) segment through scalable solutions
- Continue platform innovation and new-use-case development, building on the commercialisation track record of Trubloq, MaaP and Wisely AI over the past five years
- Leverage two decades of telecom and enterprise domain leadership, including government …

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Banks face rising phishing/fraud risks requiring scalable AI solutions | Private Sector Banks | beneficiary | High | Adoption of Wisely ATP on a per-subscriber basis creates sticky, recurring revenue; Bandhan Bank win validates cross-sell from CPaaS to Security. |
| Global telcos need compliant, localized messaging/fraud infrastructure | International Telcos | beneficiary | Med | Tanla's Indosat win demonstrates ability to deploy at scale (100M users) outside India; pipeline for more telcos is huge. |
| SMEs lack access to enterprise-grade OTT engagement tools | Indian SMEs | beneficiary | Med | Tanla targeting 2M SMEs via WhatsApp, a largely untapped market compared to saturated enterprise segment. |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Risk factors] Deck's forward-looking section flags pricing pressure and competition, customer concentration, shifts in technology standards and platform interoperability, cyber security incidents, vendor or network dependency, and adverse regulatory or judicial actions.
- [Market-size caveat] "The CPaaS industry in India is evolving rapidly, and reliable public information on the overall market remains limited" — market size and relative share figures are indicative, internal-analysis based and "should not be regarded as definitive".
- [Long-arc record] "We continue to deliver over the last Eight years": Revenues 2019 ₹10,040 Mn → 2026 ₹44,177 Mn (~4x), EBITDA ₹967 Mn → ₹7,237 Mn (~7x), PAT ₹298 Mn → ₹5,091 Mn (~17x).
